title: Model routing benchmarks, and the new Auto and Auto Code routers
gist: OpenRouter rebuilt its router and added one for coding agents. It decides every turn from eleven signals plus live price and cache state, but switches only when the gain beats the cache it gives up: in beta it kept the same model for nearly nine turns in ten. A public board runs its routers beside single models from the same pool on five public benchmarks.
changes: The comparison T8 asked for, from a router vendor. Its coding router costs 74% less than Claude Opus 5.5 at similar quality, but on Deep SWE several single models from its pool beat it on both quality and cost, and OpenRouter itself says no router beats the best single model everywhere.
caveats: Run by the vendor, on tasks others wrote. Quality on the overview chart is averaged over whichever benchmarks each entry completed, and many single-model baselines skip some, so compare per benchmark. Costs are recorded per task and the board tracks cache hits, but how cached tokens are priced is not stated. Benchmark tasks are not live sessions. Found through a post on X.
